Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks · Body, health & movement · Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

slowly adverb

also slow down, more slowly, slow

classical

lentē

adverb

festīnāre tē nōlō is Cicero’s (Fam. 16.11.1). Augustus’ “make haste slowly” was Greek, σπεῦδε βραδέως (Suet. Aug. 25; Gell. 10.11.5); festīnā lentē is the later Latin form.

Examples

  • Lentē! Festīnāre tē nōlō.

    Slowly! I don’t want you to rush.composed

  • Nōlī tantum cibī simul in ōs inserere! Lentius mandūcā!

    Don’t put so much food in your mouth at once! Chew more slowly!composed

  • lentius

    more slowlycomposed

See also eat up, firmly, run, hurry, quickly.

SourcesCicero and the Augustus note from the Latinitas loci collections.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
